core_obligations: Take a diagram of the shape required by source-and-target locality for the property at the two germs in question (proof lines 8253-8254).
Read off the resulting square of local homomorphisms of local rings between the local rings of the four schemes involved (proof lines 8255-8261).
Note that the vertical arrows are localisations of etale ring maps and hence unramified, so that the residue field extensions they induce are finite and separable (proof lines 8262-8266).
Conclude that the transcendence degrees on the two sides agree, since a finite separable extension of the base field leaves the transcendence degree unchanged (proof lines 8267-8269).
proof_roadmap: Set up the diagram required by the definition (proof lines 8253-8254).
Pass to the square of local homomorphisms of local rings (proof lines 8255-8261).
Use unramifiedness to get finite separable residue extensions (proof lines 8262-8266).
Conclude equality of transcendence degrees (proof lines 8267-8269).
difficulty_reason: For a fixed integer r, possibly infinite, the lemma asserts that the property of a morphism of germs that the residue field of the point of the source has transcendence degree r over the residue field of the image point is etale local on the source and the target (statement lines 8240-8250). The proof takes a diagram of the shape required by the definition of source-and-target locality and reads off a square of local homomorphisms of local rings, whose vertical arrows are localisations of etale ring maps and therefore unramified, so the two residue field extensions appearing there are finite separable (proof lines 8253-8266). Since a finite separable extension does not change the transcendence degree, the two sides of the asserted equality are equal, which is exactly the required invariance (proof lines 8267-8269). The claim is H2: the argument is short but complete, and it uses the etale hypothesis in a substantive way, through unramifiedness of localisations of etale ring maps and the finiteness and separability of the resulting residue field extensions.
